about.title: Union City Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Union City sits between the 880 corridor and the hills, and a lot of daily driving here funnels through the same handful of streets. Public collision records for 2025 list 179 injury crashes inside city limits, with 240 people hurt and 5 lives lost. Alvarado Niles Road, I-880, Mission Boulevard and Whipple Road carry the largest share of those reports, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 tend to be the busiest window. If one of those numbers now includes you, the next few weeks matter. California gives most drivers two years to file a claim, but far less when a city or state agency is involved, sometimes only six months. Photos, repair estimates, medical notes and witness contacts fade quickly, so gathering them early protects your position. We review car accident claims directly and can walk you through what happened before you talk to the other driver's insurer.

whyChoose.title: Why Union City Drivers Choose Us

items.title: Deadlines Handled Early
items.desc: Most California car accident claims must be filed within two years, yet a crash involving a city vehicle, a state road crew or a transit bus can shrink that window to six months. We sort out which clock applies before it becomes a problem.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so you can still recover even if you share some of the blame for a collision on Whipple Road or I-880. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of responsibility, and there is no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life.

items.title: Nothing Owed Up Front
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning no fee unless we recover for you. You also get guidance on declining the other insurer's recorded statement, which is your right.

items.question: The other driver's insurance adjuster keeps calling and wants a recorded statement. Do I have to give one?
items.answer: No. You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is generally wise to hold off until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use casual remarks about how you feel or what you remember to lower the value of your claim. You can politely tell them your attorney will be in touch.

items.question: I was hit near the Alvarado Niles Road and Mission Boulevard area. Does it matter that a Union City or Caltrans vehicle was involved?
items.answer: It matters a great deal for timing. When a government entity is a party, California generally requires a written claim within six months of the crash, far shorter than the usual two years. Missing that step can bar the case entirely, so it is worth getting the paperwork started right away. We can also help determine whether the road belongs to the city, the county or the state.

items.question: What should I save after a crash in Union City, and how can you help?
items.answer: Keep photos of the vehicles and the scene, the police report number, medical records, receipts, and the names of anyone who saw what happened. Hold on to the damaged car until it has been documented. We review your situation directly and, if we take the case, work on contingency with no fee unless there is a recovery.
